detailed_findings.finding: No substantive issues detected; the bijection and counting steps are both justified and sufficient for the stated bound.

reason: The proof gives a complete argument. It correctly proves that the inverse map I is an involution with fixed points exactly 1 and p-1, constructs the bijection phi(k)=I(k)+1 from {1,...,p-2} to {2,...,p-1}, verifies the key identity I(phi(k))=p+1-I(k+1), and deduces a bijection S ↔ A where A={b in {2,...,p-1} : I(b)+b>p+2}. It then counts A by decomposing the non-fixed points of I into 2-cycles, pairing cycle sums sigma and 2p-sigma via {u,v}↦{p-v,p-u}, excludes the exceptional sums p±2, bounds the remaining middle cases by M≤3, and concludes |A|=|S|≥(p-7)/2≥(p-1)/4=floor(p/4) for p≡5 mod 8 with p>5. No essential gaps or semantic drift were found.
